storyContext: GCAM canonical atom guidance explains how reviewers should retain the full finding while choosing a deterministic primary atom.
evidence: A single finding may map to multiple canonical atoms.
Primary atom selection should use strongest semantic match, highest severity, and clearest violation type.
Article-based clustering should give way to canonical atom clustering.
reasoning: Finding identification is not one-to-one with atom labels.
The reviewer should preserve all supported atom mappings so the finding remains complete.
The primary atom must be chosen deterministically rather than by article order.
decision: Store the finding-identification note as a universal reviewer interpretation that keeps all supported canonical atoms while selecting a deterministic primary atom.
alternativeDecisions: Treat each finding as if it can map to only one canonical atom.
Choose the primary atom by article order instead of semantic evidence.
rejectedInterpretations: One finding always equals one atom.
Article count should determine finding identity.
futureReviewNotes: If a dedicated GCAM finding-identification article or slide appears later, add it as a source-backed follow-up record.
